title: MADGER - The Open Ways World Atlas
scope: Complete foundation atlas for the eight-region story setting: 40 named characters, 14 principal communities, 9 factions, 8 encounter sites and a reproducible building system. The wider planet can grow by additive editions. This is a fictional production atlas, not a claim that every unnamed person, future adventure or architectural engineering detail exists.
authority: New owner-commissioned development. Preserves Burrow v2.1 geometry, approved hero designs and voices, and character/story revision 1.1. This edition resolves reserved exterior geography, companion origins and supporting biographies. New art is authored visual development; established hero references remain controlling.

coordinates.regional: kilometres; +X east, +Y north; Burrow Sunwell at (0,0). Z metres above Sunwell datum; vertical exaggeration prohibited in plan measurements.
coordinates.local: metres; settlement origin is its named civic anchor; +X east, +Y north, +Z up. Local points rotate 0 degrees into the regional grid.
coordinates.calendar: 360-day year, twelve 30-day months, six-day weeks. Pilot is year 0, late spring. Relative negative years count backward; no claim that these are Earth years.
coordinates.travel: Ordinary walking 24 km/day; loaded convoy 18 km/day; regional river passage 50 km/day; sea passage 90 km/day; sky passage 100 km/day in safe weather. Route days include explicit layovers where stated. No fast travel enters anime history.

regions.name: Lowland Reach
regions.environment: River terraces, reed marshes, wooded escarpments and inhabited hills; the Burrow has daylight neighborhoods and a deep civic interior.
regions.culture: Reedbank, Latchford and Millmere belong to this regional cluster. Willowmere sits toward the canopy frontier; Stonewake serves the mountain approaches. Exact road lengths await the atlas.
regions.travel_rule: Boats, footpaths and maintained crossings; spring floods alter safe passage.
regions.stories: Flood rescue, town comedy, investigation, a surface defense and a lantern-lit underground supper.
regions.creatures: Flood-wyrms are huge river animals drawn to spawning grounds; a disturbed one is dangerous without being a moral villain.

regions.name: Wandering Canopy
regions.environment: Immense trees migrate slowly between valleys during the wet season. Villages travel with some crowns; other communities stay on fixed stone ridges.
regions.culture: Local route singers preserve dated observations in practical songs; growers, climbers and instrument makers disagree about how much migration should be restrained.
regions.travel_rule: Living bridges separate as trees move. Respect the seasonal migration, local guides and climbing gear; no instantaneous forest teleportation.
regions.stories: A pursuit over folding root bridges; a harvest festival above the clouds; the missing caravan stranded between moving crowns.
regions.creatures: Mawroot blooms lure prey with warmth and a shelter-like glow. Some trees are ordinary and some predators are truly dangerous.

regions.name: Mirrorglass Expanse
regions.environment: Storm-polished glass dunes, dry salt basins and buried observatories that briefly emerge after wind scours the surface.
regions.culture: Caravan cities maintain shaded markets and rotating well access. Their history includes rival trade leagues, astronomy and water-sharing victories, not only ruins.
regions.travel_rule: Travel at safe light angles with marked water reserves. Fused glass defeats Madger’s burrowing. Mirage-glass retains brief light impressions that may be incomplete or misleading.
regions.stories: A moving sand-sail race, a night-market theft, an apparent eyewitness image with the decisive moment missing.
regions.creatures: Glassback drakes feel vibration through the dunes; they cannot be distracted by an invisible digital signal.

regions.name: Tidemark Sea
regions.environment: Reef islands and drowned civic halls exposed for short low-tide windows. Glowing shoals pass above submerged courtyards.
regions.culture: Independent harbor communities disagree over who owns objects recovered from flooded homes. Fishers, historians and salvagers have their own priorities.
regions.travel_rule: Charts, boats, breathable limits and tide clocks matter. A sunken archive can be visited only with a safe return plan.
regions.stories: An underwater heist, a rescue in a bell tower as water rises, a mystery where taking evidence damages somebody’s inheritance.
regions.creatures: Reefbacks are enormous living habitats. Hunting them for an easy resource creates consequences beyond one episode.

regions.name: Saffron Isles
regions.environment: Floating basalt landmasses above amber storm clouds, linked by cargo sails, tether lifts and occasional living vine spans.
regions.culture: Terrace farmers, sailwrights and competing sky-port councils measure wealth partly in safe landing space. Some ports welcome guests; others refuse rescue alliances.
regions.travel_rule: Natural liftstone requires local counterweights and maintenance. Flight is weather-bound; cargo and passengers have weight. Islands do not hover because of one portable crystal.
regions.stories: A vertical pursuit through a crowded sky market, a cargo race, negotiating shelter with people who value distance over connection.
regions.creatures: Storm mantas feed along charged cloud fronts. Their migration grounds sky travel even when the sky looks clear.

regions.name: Frostspine
regions.environment: Aurora-lit glaciers, warm caverns and observatories embedded in blue ice above a chain of winter settlements.
regions.culture: Winter guilds keep communal heat and weather records. Old route closures divided families, but the people now living here have ordinary art, rivalry and celebrations.
regions.travel_rule: Ropes, heat and pressure limits govern exploration. Echo-ice can retain fragments of old sound, never a complete mind or guaranteed truthful testimony.
regions.stories: A survival mystery, an ancestral argument heard out of context, deciding whether a sealed span should reopen.
regions.creatures: Choir wraiths mimic sounds they have heard to lure travelers away from shelter. They are predators, not resurrected relatives.

regions.name: Ember Steps
regions.environment: Volcanic terraces, obsidian channels, hot-spring gardens and forge towns above cooling lava shelves. The Cinder Cuts lie on its disused freight fringe.
regions.culture: Smiths, thermal gardeners and freight families compete over workable ground. Riven Claw occupies one neglected site, not the entire region.
regions.travel_rule: Heat shields, stable footing and changing gas conditions constrain travel. Useful heat is not immunity to fire.
regions.stories: A forge tournament, a rescue on a stopped freight lift, a raid seen from the people who must live beside the raiders.
regions.creatures: Ashmaws are armored burrowing predators that follow heat gradients; moving a nest may redirect a threat toward another community.

regions.name: Hollow Sea
regions.environment: Vast underground waters beneath mineral vaults, fungal shore forests and cities built on rock shelves above dark tides.
regions.culture: Deep-dwelling trading communities have their own navigation traditions and histories; surface visitors are guests. Some old passages are taboo for practical reasons.
regions.travel_rule: Mapped entry points, pressure changes, air supplies and boats matter. There is no new secret route under the Burrow’s existing defense line.
regions.stories: A luminous voyage, a missing expedition, a negotiation in darkness where the loudest voice gives away a position.
regions.creatures: Blind bell-eels hunt by vibration. Brilliant fungal blooms can be beautiful, nourishing or toxic depending on species and season.

communities.name: The Burrow
communities.appearance: A welcoming limestone basin and a larger inhabited underground town.
communities.government: Ward assemblies and shared services; Madger has no permanent veto.
communities.economy: Food gardens, workshops, care, teaching and caravan exchange. Imports salt, metals, medicine and some grain.
communities.custom: Bridge Day celebrates ordinary repairs with races, food and deliberately terrible songs. Surface and underground households exchange supper invitations.
communities.safe: Sunwell and Underhall by day; inner shelter boundary during a surface overrun.
communities.danger: No new exterior route, shaft or bypass is added to its sealed defenses.
communities.history: Six years of collective construction grew from a camp and common store into five neighborhoods. Existing footprints and route graphs are inherited verbatim.
communities.conflict: Welcome without dependence; the missing-road crisis tests whether fear will make the town surrender its values.
communities.buildings: Existing Burrow plans control all 37 primary areas and seven detailed rooms.

communities.name: Reedbank
communities.appearance: Raised river houses, terracotta roofs, timber wharves and long flood stairs.
communities.government: An elected harbor council; depot owners can petition but do not own the river.
communities.economy: Boat repair, reeds, ceramics and fish; grain arrives from the floodplain.
communities.custom: At Watermark Night families repaint their flood marks and launch harmless paper boats carrying promises they actually kept.
communities.safe: High-bank kitchen and public lofts during flood season.
communities.danger: Low wharves close in floodwater; boats follow marked channels.
communities.history: Founded 240 years ago around a ferry; survived the Severance on local river trade. The flood seven years ago scattered households and strengthened depot power.
communities.conflict: Dara and Hollis remain here. Veyra buys influence while kitchen volunteers investigate unfair allotments.

communities.name: Stonewake
communities.appearance: Occupied quarry terraces, stone arches, copper roof caps and bright workshop shutters.
communities.government: Workshop delegates, quarry residents and water crews share a three-chamber council.
communities.economy: Cut stone, metal fittings and trained builders; imports grain and timber.
communities.custom: The Unfinished Fair exhibits useful failures alongside fine craft; apprentices explain what they learned.
communities.safe: Public lower yard and braced civic galleries.
communities.danger: Old quarry faces have marked collapse zones; deep descent is licensed and physically separate from the Burrow.
communities.history: Founded 310 years ago; abandoned extraction faces were converted into homes. A work-platform failure nine years ago changed local training rules.
communities.conflict: Eris wants productive change; Oren fears rushing. Gorilla must return as a colleague rather than the one who must save everyone.
communities.buildings: Commonworks Hall|White Family Workshop|Deep Descent House

communities.name: Latchford
communities.appearance: A bustling junction town of inns, arcades, wagon courts and public dispatch boards.
communities.government: Rotating neighborhood council and an independent route tribunal.
communities.economy: Transport, repair, lodging and records; reliable information is an export.
communities.custom: The Six Roads Supper seats strangers by destination, not rank. Stories are traded before prices.
communities.safe: Accord courtyard and staffed arrival houses.
communities.danger: An unfamiliar seal is checked against a second source; private rented rooms are not automatic criminal sites.
communities.history: Grew around three roads 180 years ago. The Severance made it a transfer hub; relay trade arrived 38 years ago.
communities.conflict: Glass Thread rents limited rooms here. Honest dispatchers resent outsiders treating the whole town as a den of criminals.
communities.buildings: Accord Convoy House|Six Roads Inn|North Relay Rooms

communities.name: Millmere
communities.appearance: Working canals, painted mill wheels, brick workshops and narrow planted bridges.
communities.government: Canal wards elect stewards; worker cooperatives operate many workshops.
communities.economy: Paper, instruments, small machines and food milling; imports ore and hardwood.
communities.custom: During Wheelstill Day every mill stops for inspection, music and races using hand-powered toy boats.
communities.safe: Canal schools and elevated public bridges.
communities.danger: Wheel pits and locked sluice works are industrial hazards, not secret monster entrances.
communities.history: A mill settlement for 220 years. Unequal restoration after a flood pushed some young residents away; Nix learned to distrust official accounts.
communities.conflict: Lume wants Bot to visit without feeling summoned. Nix tries to turn old neglect into permission to injure new strangers.

communities.name: Willowmere
communities.appearance: Orchard lanes, rain gardens, low timber teaching halls and the first enormous canopy roots.
communities.government: Growing circles and household delegates; water decisions are recorded publicly.
communities.economy: Fruit, seeds, dyes and local guides; imports tools and salt.
communities.custom: Seed Exchange pairs every rare seed with the story of who kept it alive. Children invent impossible plants in clay.
communities.safe: Teaching courtyards and the fixed ridge path.
communities.danger: Migration-season root corridors are closed at dusk until guides inspect them.
communities.history: Founded 145 years ago by growers and guides at the forest margin. It stayed small by choice rather than isolation.
communities.conflict: Neri and Sori disagree about returning; each has relatives and responsibilities in two places.
communities.buildings: Seed House|Ridge Teaching Hall|Canopy Guide Lodge

communities.name: Cinder Cuts
communities.appearance: Old freight cuttings, exposed basalt terraces, repaired worker homes and abandoned sidings.
communities.government: Three occupied terraces maintain a residents council; Riven Claw occupies only the disused eastern spur.
communities.economy: Salvage, hauling and ceramic repair; independent workers trade with Kettle Crown.
communities.custom: The Last Whistle fair honors retired engines with percussion and shared food.
communities.safe: Occupied west terraces and public worker hostel.
communities.danger: Eastern Spur is controlled by Riven Claw; steam trenches and unstable freight edges are marked.
communities.history: Built 75 years ago as a freight district after the Severance. A route diversion 18 years ago reduced work; raiders arrived seven years ago.
communities.conflict: Dreg has family in the legitimate neighborhood. Brakka tries to turn neglected workers into a captive supply base.

communities.name: Crownrest
communities.appearance: A settlement on six colossal living crowns, joined by adjustable bridges above a fixed stone ridge.
communities.government: Each crown chooses a delegate; bridge crews can suspend a crossing despite a festival timetable.
communities.economy: Resin craft, living fiber, medicine plants and route guidance; grains are stored in the fixed ridge depot.
communities.custom: The Returning Shade festival reunites crowns after migration; dancers adjust tempo to swaying branches.
communities.safe: Fixed Ridge House during storms; tethered crown decks in normal weather.
communities.danger: A drifting crown changes its local position by up to 180 m during wet season; the baseline plan records spring anchor positions.
communities.history: Founded 160 years ago by orchard people and canopy guides. Its architecture moves with trees rather than forcing roots to stand still.
communities.conflict: Senn knows a route that records call abandoned. Saving outsiders may expose a shelter his community promised to keep quiet.

communities.name: Ossara
communities.appearance: A sandstone city of shaded courts, wind towers, turquoise shutters and glass dunes beyond its walls.
communities.government: Public well assemblies and craft wards; the Salt Crown company is a powerful rival, not the government.
communities.economy: Optical glass, salt, astronomy and caravan goods; roof cisterns and three seasonal aquifers support agriculture.
communities.custom: The Night of Two Shadows uses lanterns and mirrored sails for street theater; guests must bring a story, not a gift.
communities.safe: Public cistern courts and deep caravan inns.
communities.danger: Dune travel stops during glass storms; reflected light is not a reliable navigation bearing.
communities.history: Founded 420 years ago at three wells. An old observatory survived the Severance, but its archives preserve only fragments.
communities.conflict: Maela discovers some water debts are fabricated. Kavar sells stability while deliberately keeping a competing well closed.
communities.buildings: Three Wells Court|Mirror Observatory|Salt Crown Counting House

communities.name: Nacre Quay
communities.appearance: A coral-colored port wrapped around stepped tidal basins and limestone arcades.
communities.government: Harbor crews, salvage families and reef tenders elect a tide council.
communities.economy: Sailing, salt fish, reef gardening and salvage; fresh water comes from roof collection and inland springs.
communities.custom: Low Tide Theater stages plays on steps exposed for only an hour; everyone helps strike the stage before water returns.
communities.safe: Upper quay, rescue house and marked moorings.
communities.danger: The drowned archive opens only around low tide; reefback migration closes the outer channel seasonally.
communities.history: Founded 280 years ago above an older drowned district. The sinking preceded the Severance; neither event caused the other.
communities.conflict: Toma must choose between a profitable salvage claim and evidence belonging to living descendant communities.
communities.buildings: Tide Council Hall|Rescue Sail House|Drowned Archive

communities.name: Aurel Quay
communities.appearance: Three floating basalt islands joined by cargo spans, with counterweights, hanging gardens and ochre sails.
communities.government: Independent dock cooperatives and neighborhood crews; no captain owns an island.
communities.economy: Weather routing, liftstone shaping and sail making; food arrives by cargo craft and terrace gardens.
communities.custom: Weight Day is a comedy festival where teams build the lightest absurd object that still performs its job.
communities.safe: Sheltered inner moorings and grounded storm refuges on each island.
communities.danger: Liftstone responds to local fields, with strict load budgets; it cannot be carried elsewhere to float arbitrary cities.
communities.history: Established 130 years ago around seasonal anchor fields. Its first charter outlawed selling residents with a vessel.
communities.conflict: Eri refuses a lucrative overloaded launch. Serik offers stranded crews a rescue that becomes a protection racket.

communities.name: Hushvale
communities.appearance: A geothermal town under a glacier shoulder, with copper roof caps, steam gardens and blue ice light.
communities.government: Winter guilds and household delegates share stores; the archive order holds expertise, not unlimited civil authority.
communities.economy: Insulation cloth, cold storage, optical ice study and mountain guiding.
communities.custom: The Quiet Hour marks storms survived; the following feast is deliberately noisy and full of imitation bird calls.
communities.safe: Warm civic cavern and staffed wayhouses.
communities.danger: Echo ice can repeat old sounds; choirwraith habitat is mapped beyond the warm ridge.
communities.history: Founded 360 years ago around springs. Routekeepers here cut resonance links during the Severance and inherited both gratitude and blame.
communities.conflict: Ysolde finds a true warning mixed with a forged prohibition. Ossa cannot accept that stewardship requires other people to judge the evidence.

communities.name: Kettle Crown
communities.appearance: A city on volcanic shelves, with obsidian stairs, red ceramic roofs and lush hot-spring gardens.
communities.government: Forge cooperatives, growers and freight neighborhoods negotiate heat and water shares.
communities.economy: Ceramics, tempered metal and heat-grown fruit; imports timber and cool-water crops.
communities.custom: The Cooling Feast celebrates a finished kiln cycle; rival makers exchange deliberately ridiculous cups.
communities.safe: Stone civic courts and supervised hot-spring gardens.
communities.danger: Gas troughs and active channels close under marked conditions; lava is not casually crossed by being brave.
communities.history: Founded 190 years ago on old cooled shelves. Industrial growth enriched the city while the diverted freight line harmed Cinder Cuts.
communities.conflict: Kesh must acknowledge the town profited from a decision that hurt its neighbors without accepting Brakka as their representative.
communities.buildings: Common Kiln Hall|Spring Garden House|Freight Mediation Hall

communities.name: Lumen Tide
communities.appearance: A vertical limestone city above a subterranean ocean, with mineral windows and fungal shore gardens.
communities.government: Harbor, air and food circles elect rotating speakers; surface visitors follow local law.
communities.economy: Fungal textiles, mineral instruments and cavern navigation; imports grains through Stonewake trade.
communities.custom: The Lantern Descent lowers lamps to remember people who left on voyages; it ends with dancing, not a funeral.
communities.safe: Ventilated upper civic terraces and inspected refuge docks.
communities.danger: Pressure, air quality and sea level determine access; no passage connects it directly to the Burrow.
communities.history: A continuous community for at least 600 years, with several written founding traditions. Its oldest harbor predates the Open Ways.
communities.conflict: Namu wants surface partnership on equal terms. A rediscovered chart threatens to invite extractive expeditions into sacred nesting waters.
communities.buildings: Tide Speakers Hall|Fungal Exchange|Pressure Gate House

characters.contradiction: Confuses daring rescue and being needed with reliable leadership.
characters.relationships: Gorilla, Bot and Snow are partners with distinct agency; Sela concealed Veyra’s rescue funding; Nix knows him before he became a founder.

blocks.text: MADGER
Character 001 • The founder and the broken roads
Approved likeness reference. Its illustrated setting does not add a new location to the map.
Identity: male stylized badger • 24 at the pilot • born in Reedbank • founder, organizer and explorer • Burrow Commons (FAC-01).
Home: west end of the +12 m Hearth Terraces tier (BRW-03), shared with Snow White. Regular places: Sunwell, Common House and the town’s work sites.
Core desire: build a home worth returning to, then bring back the people stranded beyond its protection. Core need: trust others with decisions and face truths that complicate his own heroic story.
Contradiction: he wants everyone safe, yet loves the thrill of the unknown. He is ashamed of how much he sometimes wants to leave the place he built.
“We can be afraid when we get back. Right now, we need a way across.”
Character-development edition 1.1 • 20 October 2026 • Fantasy-adventure revision. Includes writer-only future reveals; approved appearance and voice retained.
01  The person beneath the founder

Madger is quick to laugh, quicker to volunteer, and uneasy when everyone else is working while he sits still. He remembers which doorway sticks and who likes the end piece of a loaf. He often learns a stranger’s practical problem before learning their surname. His welcome feels personal because he pays attention.

He loves being needed and being first over a difficult crossing. Curiosity makes him inventive; applause can make him reckless. Under pressure he moves faster, dismisses unfamiliar local knowledge and offers certainty before he has earned it. His hardest mistake is confusing a daring rescue with a plan that keeps people safe afterward.

His deepest fear is returning to an empty place where people trusted him to come back. His private temptation is escape: an unexplored horizon asks less of him than a town full of people he loves. He must learn to leave responsibly and return without pretending every journey made him wiser than those who stayed.
A life beyond the mission

He likes toasted root buns, improvised tabletop games and listening to the different sounds of the town waking up. He collects small useful offcuts for repairs; Jun insists that half his collection is merely clutter. He enjoys playful contests with Gorilla and usually loses the contests that require patience.

At home he leaves a clear resting place for Snow and talks through his day while she settles. He writes to Dara and Hollis in Reedbank, including ordinary successes rather than only emergencies. A quiet meal is genuinely satisfying to him, even when learning to stay for it is difficult.
Values, boundaries and failure

He will protect a visitor before asking whether that visitor can repay him. He will not knowingly abandon a trapped person, punish a whole group for one member’s crime, or treat Bot as property. He can still make harmful choices: conceal exhaustion, promise access too early, or dismiss a careful objection as unnecessary delay. When wrong, repair must include an apology, a changed decision and a practical cost he accepts.
02  The boy who promised a way out

Madger grew up in Reedbank, where floodplain houses stand above boat channels and river fog catches the light of old wayposts. Dara, his mother, organized a neighborhood kitchen; Hollis, his father, repaired working boats. Both are alive and still live there. Their stories of distant travelers made the world feel enormous. Their work taught him that someone always has to mend the boat after the adventure.

As teenagers, Madger and Nix Vey explored abandoned towpaths and built unreliable little river craft. Nix, from Millmere, spent work seasons around Reedbank’s repair yards. Madger wanted to discover safe routes; Nix wanted to prove that the people controlling those routes were less clever than they claimed. Their friendship was affectionate, competitive and already divided over whether a good result excused a dishonest method.

Seven years before the pilot, a natural flood drowned Reedbank’s lower streets. Seventeen-year-old Madger promised eighteen households passage before checking the convoy’s capacity. Several had to wait until the following day. All eighteen households survived. Sela Venn organized the second departure and made him help with the work. On the flooded towpath he learned that a courageous promise can still leave somebody stranded.

The flood dispersed his circle. Nix returned toward Millmere, bitter at the authorities who decided whose neighborhood was worth restoring. Madger spent the following year helping displaced people seek a durable home. Neither friend was secretly imprisoned or presumed dead. They made different choices and gradually stopped writing.

At eighteen, six years before the pilot, Madger helped a voluntary group establish the first camp and common store at the future Burrow. Many surveyors, builders and families created the town in stages. He wanted a refuge that would welcome a person before asking which powerful patron stood behind them. He also wanted to build something Nix could no longer dismiss as another empty promise.

Veyra Kest offered exclusive supply terms during that first year. Madger nearly accepted, then withdrew after the community debated the cost. What he does not yet know: Veyra had paid to charter Reedbank’s second evacuation convoy. Then a depot manager, she diverted company reserves without her partners’ approval and demanded anonymity to protect her position. Sela agreed to get people out, then kept quiet from shame and fear of losing their trust. Veyra’s help was real; her later claim that it entitles her to control the Burrow is not.

By the pilot Madger is twenty-four. The Burrow is a thriving, collectively built town with the existing 2,400-resident planning baseline. Beyond it lie lost roads, independent peoples and living landscapes he has never seen. His first great adventure was finding a home. His next begins when people on the roads to that home stop arriving.
03  The people who change him

Gorilla White — building partner and closest friend. They first worked together during the Burrow’s first year, bracing a work platform before a rainstorm. Gorilla refused Madger’s unsafe shortcut; Madger stayed to finish the slower job. Each recognizes the other’s habit of carrying too much. Their friendship deepens when they stop praising one another for exhaustion.

MADGER Bot — colleague with independent judgment. Bot joined the town five years before the pilot and chose records and maintenance work. Madger first values the speed of Bot’s answers; later he learns to value “I cannot confirm that.” Bot’s maker and earlier history belong in Bot’s card. Madger neither owns Bot nor has authority to override Bot’s consent.

Snow White — companion, never a talking accessory. Three years before the pilot, an adult Snow arrived with a Wayfarer crew whose handler was retiring. A gradual, mutually comfortable placement led to her home with Madger. She is six at the pilot. He learns to notice her pause, posture and return, then verify what caused them. She can detect a physical scent or sound, not a digital intrusion or a person’s moral character.

Mara and Jun — neighbors who expose his ordinary flaws. Mara mirrors his overcommitting; Jun challenges the claim that every unfinished task is an emergency. They can refuse him without becoming disloyal.

Iona and Pell — necessary disagreement. Iona demands evidence that a plan is workable. Pell asks whether a newcomer can understand it. Madger’s growth means giving both a real voice before promising an outcome.

Sela Venn — trusted rescuer with a damaging omission. She helped the frightened seventeen-year-old and remains willing to contradict him. Her silence about Veyra’s rescue funding was a deliberate choice, not a forgotten detail. When he learns the truth, their trust must be rebuilt through disclosure and action. Dara and Hollis remain loving, ordinary parents, not concealed rulers or custodians of a destined bloodline.

Veyra Kest — benefactor and adversary. Madger knows her as the merchant director whose exclusive supply terms he rejected. He does not know she funded the flood’s second evacuation convoy. The discovery forces him to acknowledge a real good act while opposing her current coercion. She offers the temptation he finds hardest to resist: certainty, purchased with somebody else’s freedom.

Nix Vey — the friend who took another road. Madger remembers their shared boats, dares and arguments; he does not know Nix now leads Glass Thread. He will initially excuse signs of manipulation because he wants the friendship back. Nix’s wish to expose injustice is sincere, and their willingness to endanger strangers is equally real. A rescue or apology cannot settle that debt.

Knowledge at the pilot: Madger knows Nix as an estranged friend, Veyra as a rejected supplier and Sela as a rescuer. He does not know Glass Thread’s membership, the hidden rescue funding, or who is probing Burrow records. These are writer-only facts until their scheduled reveals.
04  Abilities that have a cost

Social skill: he makes an intimidating task feel possible and invites people into it. This works best when he explains the need and listens. It fails when enthusiasm obscures limits or makes saying no feel unkind.

Physical skill: agile, observant and experienced at navigating familiar ground. BURROW crosses designated diggable soil with a visible entry, dirt trail and emergence. On glass dunes, suspended islands, deep water or solid ice it cannot provide an easy exit. He needs local knowledge, equipment and teammates. Stone, pipes, foundations and occupied rooms remain barriers; new environments do not silently rewrite game statistics.

Practical skill: basic repairs, climbing, route preparation and improvising with ordinary gear. He can learn regional waycraft, the practice of working with unusual materials and living terrain, but begins as a novice. A borrowed sail, living-root crossing or signal instrument requires instruction and can fail. He has no unique bloodline key, unlimited magic or power that makes other people’s expertise unnecessary.
Stress, performance and voice

In comfort: open shoulders, attentive ears, unforced smile, compact gestures. In doubt: a brief pause, glance toward the person with relevant expertise, paws momentarily still. Under pressure: shortened sentences and a tendency to move before the briefing ends. He becomes decisive by taking a breath and asking a precise question, not through a transformation or new power.

Use the approved Excited Teen R2 performance and ElevenLabs voice OvSI8qvaDkaFiIdSCWRw. His youthful energy remains compatible with his newly authored age of 24. Do not select a replacement voice or alter the approved processing to make him sound older. New dialogue is written for that existing performance.

Dialogue is direct, warm and occasionally playful. He asks names, uses specific offers and admits when he missed something. He avoids speeches that make neighbors sound like followers. Useful lines: “I said I could do it. I forgot to ask whether I should do it alone.” / “Close the inner gate when the checks say to. We can welcome people without pretending there is no danger.”
Visual continuity

Retain the approved black-and-cream likeness, black belly, high cream chest V, natural arms, stable proportions and small even teeth. No oversized fang or decorative tear beneath the eye. Sweat, injury or dirt appears only when the scene justifies it and is tracked between shots. The approved reference is a likeness source; its background is not evidence of an additional tunnel, room or vehicle in the world.
05  The Missing Roads

Season-one story: a travelling group bound for the Burrow disappears from a trusted route. Madger follows the trail into a forest whose great trees migrate between valleys. Someone has been changing route reports, turning places of safety into places travelers cannot find. His search brings him back to Nix, now a gifted information criminal working with people who profit from dependence.

Pilot: a joyful ordinary day wholly inside the Burrow, above and below ground. Madger’s impatience produces a small comic complication, then a shared success. Bot retains the anomalous D17 duplicate receipt; Snow notices a separate physical scent. End on a moment of quiet unease. No villain reveal, attack, exterior cutaway or ancient-history speech.

Departure: a later missed caravan turns the small irregularity into a personal obligation. Madger leaves with a stated rescue objective and a capable team at home. He finds Nix in a canopy settlement and mistakes familiar humor for renewed trust. His longing for the old friendship blinds him more effectively than a disguise.

Midpoint: an unmistakably familiar bit of improvised equipment links Nix to a forged route instruction. Nix admits leading Glass Thread. Their public grievance is genuine: some communities have been erased from trade maps. Their private crime is using vulnerable travelers as leverage to force that grievance into view. Madger chooses the stranded families over pursuing Nix and loses evidence as a result.

Reversal: back home, proof that Veyra funded the second flood convoy shatters his tidy division between rescuers and exploiters. Sela admits her silence. Veyra uses the revelation to press for control of the Burrow’s supply routes. Madger thanks her for the rescue and still refuses her demand. Gratitude gives her a hearing, not ownership.

Climax: Brakka raids the surface for supplies while the Burrow deals with disrupted outside communications. Brakka is pursuing her own opportunity, not obeying Veyra’s secret master plan. Madger must accept protective inner closures and a rescue role. Gorilla, Bot, Snow and trained residents each solve problems he cannot solve. Nix helps stop one consequence of their intrusion, then escapes; one good action does not redeem the whole crew.

Resolution: the missing travelers reach safety and the immediate raid is repelled. The town repairs damage, disputes the next step and chooses to support a small outward rescue partnership. Madger finally tells the complete story of the flood and gives others credit. The wider adventure begins through an earned decision, not an unresolved cliffhanger that withholds the season’s promised rescue.
06  Beyond this first season

Madger’s development continues in a larger world. In the Mirrorglass Expanse he cannot dig his way out and must follow a local guide. Beneath the Tidemark Sea he must choose between preserving evidence and rescuing an enemy. Among the Saffron Isles he encounters people who do not want the Burrow’s protection. In Frostspine he learns that reopening an old road can restore contact and awaken an old danger at the same time.

His lasting growth is from wanting to be the answer to helping others make real choices. He remains funny, adventurous and capable of poor judgment. Protecting the Burrow does not require every story to threaten it. Some journeys concern another community’s mystery, a race, a monster, a discovery or a friend’s unfinished business.

Scene test — wonder: he laughs while riding a cargo platform through migrating treetops, then realizes the local guide has stopped smiling.
Scene test — betrayal: Nix repeats the joke they used to make before a reckless jump; this time Madger notices who is standing below.
Scene test — growth: he returns home to find that a problem he worried about was solved without him, and asks how they did it.

Revision note: this edition explicitly replaces the earlier statement that Madger has no knowledge of Nix. He knows the old friend, not the current criminal identity. It also replaces the mainly civic season outline with the missing-caravan adventure. His age, parents, natural flood, eighteen surviving households, founding date, companion meeting anchors, approved voice and likeness remain unchanged.

factions.name: Burrow Commons
factions.purpose: Keep a welcoming town livable, fair and defensible. This names the civic cooperation already present in the Bible; it does not replace ward decisions with a new ruler.
factions.leadership: Ward delegates, open meetings and rotating work coordinators. Madger convenes and serves; his founder status gives him no permanent veto. Snow is a protected companion, not an office-holder.
factions.methods: Shared stores, maintenance rosters, public explanations, rescue practice and accountable protective closures. Disputes concern priorities and evidence, not whether ordinary residents deserve safety.
factions.tension: Welcome versus capacity. Pell wants understandable procedures; Iona wants verified limits; Madger sometimes promises both before consulting either.
factions.ties: Commonworks supplies expertise; the Wayfarer Accord brings visitors and goods. The Commons opposes coercion by the Gilt Ledger, intrusion by Glass Thread and predation by Riven Claw.

factions.name: Commonworks Fellowship
factions.home: Stonewake and a regional workshop network
factions.purpose: Make essential knowledge teachable so no settlement depends on one indispensable specialist.
factions.leadership: Oren Vale coordinates exchanges. Iona is the Burrow contact; Tavi is an apprentice participant, never an unsupervised emergency specialist.
factions.methods: Travelling repair crews, apprenticeships, shared specifications and tool loans. Each town keeps local authority over its own machinery.
factions.tension: Their careful standards can postpone urgent improvisation. Oren must learn when a temporary repair is responsible, while Madger must accept when it is unsafe.
factions.ties: Works with the Commons and Wayfarers. Refuses exclusive maintenance deals from the Gilt Ledger. Glass Thread can steal records, but cannot acquire practical mastery by downloading them.

factions.name: Wayfarer Accord
factions.home: Latchford; independent crews across the road network
factions.purpose: Keep travel, rescue and honest exchange possible for people without powerful sponsors.
factions.leadership: Sela Venn coordinates convoy safety. Lark Quill carries dispatches and keeps route accounts. Crews can decline a route they cannot safely serve.
factions.methods: Guides, escorted caravans, weather reports and voluntary rescue agreements. Their wagons are finite; an invitation does not create transport capacity.
factions.tension: Keeping a promised timetable may conflict with stopping for strangers. Sela supports Madger but will not endorse a comforting promise she cannot fulfill.
factions.ties: Supplies the Burrow and transports Commonworks crews. Pays legitimate tolls, contests Gilt Ledger coercion, and resists Riven Claw raids. Lark occasionally buys information from Pip Skein.

factions.name: Gilt Ledger
factions.home: Privately controlled warehouses and offices in Reedbank
factions.purpose: Make independent settlements reliant on its depots, credit and permission to trade. Its public promise is dependable supply; its private objective is lasting leverage.
factions.leadership: Director Veyra Kest sets policy. Corvin Silt brokers contracts and influence. Bale Nacre controls stock, transport allocations and collections.
factions.methods: Exclusive supply terms, selective shortages, pressure on indebted operators and purchased information. It owns particular businesses, not Reedbank or every merchant.
factions.tension: Veyra calls dependence stability. Corvin profits from ambiguity; Bale knows that a frightened workforce eventually stops cooperating.
factions.ties: Buys limited information jobs from Glass Thread through Corvin. It has no command over the hacker crew. It sometimes buys stolen goods through intermediaries but regards Riven Claw as an expensive disruption.

factions.name: Glass Thread
factions.purpose: Sell privileged information and turn uncertain records into influence. Members claim that exposing weak systems excuses exploiting the people who rely on them.
factions.leadership: Nix Vey chooses targets and negotiates jobs. Tessera Keen handles social access and forged identities. Patch Serein maintains stolen equipment and relays.
factions.methods: Fictional record tampering, impersonation and constrained system intrusions. Access requires a particular opportunity; local controls, human checks and physical barriers still matter.
factions.tension: Nix wants recognition; Tessera wants profitable anonymity; Patch wants an exit before someone is physically harmed. Remorse does not erase responsibility.
factions.ties: Accepts selected Gilt Ledger contracts and keeps its own secrets. Distrusts Riven Claw, whose violence destroys useful contacts. Writer-only v1.1 answer: Tessera’s limited relay probe causes D17. Madger does not know Glass Thread’s membership at the pilot; Snow’s scent is unrelated.

factions.name: Riven Claw
factions.home: Disused freight terraces in the Cinder Cuts
factions.purpose: Extract supplies and obedience from travellers and weaker outposts. Its leader treats possession as something proved through force.
factions.leadership: Brakka Mourn commands raids. Dreg Husk controls hauling and shares. Vessa Rake scouts routes and bargains for intelligence.
factions.methods: Ambush, intimidation and theft of movable supplies. They need food, rest, transport and local knowledge; they cannot appear anywhere without a route.
factions.tension: Brakka prizes spectacle, Dreg wants sustainable provisions, and Vessa resents being treated as expendable. Their cooperation depends on rewards and fear.
factions.ties: Sells through fences including Pip, who can refuse a deal. It has occasional transactions with Gilt Ledger intermediaries, no standing alliance. No species is inherently loyal to this band.

factions.name: Free Harbors Compact
factions.home: A treaty among Crownrest, Ossara public wells, Nacre Quay, Aurel Quay and Lumen Tide; no capital
factions.purpose: Protect passage, rescue rights and local ownership of knowledge without turning mutual aid into annexation.
factions.leadership: Rotating local delegates; any new obligation requires the affected community’s consent.
factions.methods: Reciprocal refuge, shared weather observations and narrowly scoped archive exchanges.
factions.tension: Secrecy protects some communities but can endanger visiting travelers. Wealthier ports try to dominate timetables.
factions.ties: Works with Wayfarers and Commonworks. Opposes water coercion, sky ransom and extraction without agreement.

factions.name: Blackwake Sails

factions.purpose: Turn emergency passage into permanent tribute.
factions.leadership: Serik commands three small cargo craft; captains bargain over shares and can desert.
factions.methods: False promises, seized cargo and ransom; real rescue skill makes the deception credible.
factions.tension: Crew members want profit and survival, not Serik’s theater of heroism.
factions.ties: Occasional trade with Riven Claw; no global villain command structure. Eri knows their procedures.

factions.name: Still Bell Archive

factions.purpose: Preserve Severance evidence and assess dangerous resonant crossings.

factions.tension: Real expertise can become a monopoly on judgment. Most archivists are neither villains nor infallible sages.
factions.ties: Needs independent Hollow Sea records; disputed by Free Harbors; Commonworks can test physical claims.

history.truth: Independent deep-water oral and written traditions describe a harbor civilization; no surface dynasty is made its founder.
Three caravanning groups settle around distinct wells; their agreements become the basis of later public claims.
Spring caverns support a permanent mountain community and early weather observation.
Working quarries and shelter galleries become a town; later construction preserves some dangerous abandoned faces.
A new port grows above an older drowned district. The submergence is a separate geological event, not the Severance.
Boat crews and riverside households establish shared flood stairs and public food stores.
Milling and instrument crafts establish a canal community.
Local builders connect bridges, shelters, signals and limited waycraft. Exclusion and toll disputes exist alongside cooperation.
Cooled volcanic shelves and managed springs support a forge-and-garden settlement.
Three maintained roads create a transfer town and a culture of route testimony.
Canopy communities establish adjustable crown decks and a fixed ridge refuge.
Growers settle the forest margin; seeds and teaching become shared institutions.
Mooring communities adopt cooperative load rules and prohibit ownership of residents through vessel contracts.
A resonance-span cascade threatens connected crossings. Routekeepers deliberately cut some couplings to prevent wider collapse. Other roads fail later through weather, conflict and neglect.
Some closed routes are necessary; others remain closed because toll interests and fearful institutions benefit. No single actor controls the whole network.
New freight terraces provide work, then grow into mixed households and repair shops.
A new line enriches Kettle Crown and reduces Cinder Cuts work. Political decisions, not a monster attack, create this grievance.
Nineteen-year-old Gorilla tries to hold a failing work platform rather than insisting on evacuation. Eris is injured and recovers; responsibility is recorded.
Lume and the Millmere cooperative build a learning maintenance person. Agency grows through relationships and choices.
Madger overpromises transport for eighteen households; a second convoy saves everyone. Veyra’s concealed funding and Sela’s agreement become a later revelation.
Madger and a voluntary group establish a camp and common store. Surveyors and builders document existing rock, water and entries before expansion. Gorilla joins in the first year.

history.event: Bot joins; first major inhabited galleries
history.truth: Bot chooses records and maintenance work. Iona’s later team inherits documented systems, not a forgotten magical machine.
Workshops, food exchange, teaching and care expand with households; Mara, Jun and Edda arrive through ordinary work and family decisions.
Asha retires. Gradual placement with Madger succeeds, with continuing visits. Occupied underground wards expand within surveyed allocations.
An apprentice household settles West Deep. The town is established enough to give younger residents ambitions beyond survival.
Late spring. Two populated districts, 2,400 planning residents, public access and independent inner defenses. The repaired bridge is sound. Joy precedes subtle clues.

burrow_construction.work: Camp, survey, common store and temporary work platforms. Existing rock galleries are mapped before habitation. No ancient machine creates the town.
Surface housing and civic services grow alongside the first reinforced inhabited galleries. Water, air, waste and access are installed before each occupancy increment.
Four underground wards and shared civic rooms reach the present layout. Builders reuse documented connections; no undisclosed bypass is invented.
All 37 primary areas and seven detailed subplans match v2.1. The town maintains rather than magically expands its capacity.

waycraft.name: Resonant spans
waycraft.rule: Coupled stone and metal structures can share loads only within a measured local frequency and material condition. Damage can propagate through a coupled chain. Cutting a coupling stops transmission but closes that route.
waycraft.cost: Inspection, tuned materials and locally powered mechanisms; reconnection is a tested engineering choice, not a spell.

waycraft.name: Canopy shaping
waycraft.rule: Slow cultivation encourages living fibers; full bridges take growing seasons. Guide songs encode timing and work sequences, not mind control.
waycraft.cost: Water, trained care and seasonal limits. Fire or rapid cutting permanently damages a tree.

waycraft.name: Mirage glass
waycraft.rule: Certain glass layers retain partial light impressions under rare conditions. They show fragments from an angle, without sound, intent or guaranteed dates.
waycraft.cost: Careful extraction, controlled light and comparison with independent evidence.

waycraft.name: Liftstone
waycraft.rule: Specific basalt inclusions respond to local field zones in the Saffron Isles. Load, anchor field and weather determine stable altitude.
waycraft.cost: Counterweights and inspection; ore moved beyond a field does not float freely.

waycraft.name: Echo ice
waycraft.rule: Layered mineral ice stores and repeats sound fragments under pressure changes. Sounds can overlap or be misordered.
waycraft.cost: Cold preservation and expert interpretation; no resurrection or reading minds.

waycraft.name: Ordinary technology
waycraft.rule: Relays, instruments and local networks coexist with hand tools and sail transport. A message is a claim; a physical latch is independent.
waycraft.cost: Power, maintenance, specific access and local knowledge. No universal instant map or hacking power.

everyday_world.text: Communities are mixed-species societies. Species affects anatomy and some needs, never moral allegiance. Mechanical persons have agency. Ordinary animals such as Snow and wildlife remain distinct from anthropomorphic citizens. No human population is introduced in this edition.

Grains, roots, fruits, cultivated fungi, legumes and regional fish support distinct cuisines. Cargo has weight and spoilage. Each community’s imports explain its partnerships; no city survives solely by selling secrets. Fictional small coin and barter appear without tying plot prices to a real token.

Households include relatives, chosen family, apprentices and solitary residents. A home has privacy, storage, food preparation and a way to receive visitors. New arrivals come for work, affection, curiosity and retirement as well as displacement.

A common trade tongue permits travel, while local names, songs and technical terms need interpretation. Writing is widespread but not universal. Records, oral histories and physical evidence can disagree without making an entire culture dishonest.

Communities hold different beliefs about rivers, ancestors, stars and the deep sea. No narrator proves a single religion correct. Festivals can be joyful, comic or solemn and need not conceal a villain.

Local councils, tribunals and craft agreements differ. Captured offenders face community-specific proceedings rather than automatic execution. Good institutions can make mistakes; enemies may tell truths. No faction represents every member of a species or region.

The inhabited atlas spans hundreds of kilometres and large height differences. A voyage creates separation, missed news and new relationships. Strange environments have economies and children and meals, not only dangers waiting for heroes.

The pilot remains entirely inside the Burrow and shows no villain identity. New geography becomes available afterward. Each scene records location, route, elapsed time, knowledge, injuries, resources and changes. Game retries are not historical resurrection.

seasons.title: The Missing Roads
seasons.question: Can a welcoming home defend itself without becoming dependent on someone else’s power?

episodes.title: A Day Worth Keeping
episodes.plot: Warmth, play and competence; D17 duplicate receipt and Snow’s unrelated scent create two small pauses.
episodes.character_turn: Madger accepts help with an ordinary task. No attack or named villain reveal.

episodes.title: The Wagon That Did Not Arrive
episodes.plot: A missed arrival has real people attached to it. Two independent reports disagree; a legitimate delay becomes a rescue inquiry.
episodes.character_turn: Madger states what he knows and leaves a functioning team at home.

episodes.title: Where the Road Walks
episodes.plot: A local guide leads the group onto moving crowns. A familiar joke announces Nix’s return before the criminal connection is known.
episodes.character_turn: His longing for the old friendship weakens his judgment.

episodes.title: The Wrong Way Home
episodes.plot: A forged route instruction draws travelers toward a closing bridge. Bot compares the instruction with physical travel conditions; Snow locates a real trail.
episodes.character_turn: Madger corrects a confident error publicly and accepts the guide’s route.

episodes.title: Someone Below
episodes.plot: Nix’s distinctive improvised equipment exposes the link to Glass Thread. Madger can pursue the fleeing friend or secure the travelers below.
episodes.character_turn: He chooses the rescue and loses the best portable evidence; the choice changes the investigation.

episodes.title: The Price of Rescue
episodes.plot: A charter record and the surviving boat operator independently establish Veyra’s flood funding. Sela admits her deliberate omission.
episodes.character_turn: Madger can acknowledge an enemy’s good act without accepting her control.

episodes.title: An Offer at the Gate
episodes.plot: Veyra offers dependable supply in return for exclusive control. Brakka learns that strained outside routes have concentrated stores in the Burrow.
episodes.character_turn: Madger gives residents the complete information before they decide.

episodes.title: Above and Below
episodes.plot: Brakka’s independent raid begins. Public spaces evacuate; physical inner defenses hold while contradictory outside messages complicate the response.
episodes.character_turn: Madger follows a role assigned by the defense plan rather than inventing a private rescue mission.

episodes.title: Hold the Way
episodes.plot: Gorilla protects a retreat, Bot verifies local signals, Snow finds stranded travelers and Madger secures the final crossing. Nix helps stop one consequence of the intrusion but escapes accountability for the rest.
episodes.character_turn: The missing group arrives through teamwork and local expertise; Brakka’s immediate raid fails.

episodes.title: A Place to Return To
episodes.plot: Recovery, disagreement, thanks and a shared meal. Evidence points toward other erased refuge routes; residents choose a limited outward rescue partnership.
episodes.character_turn: Resolve the missing caravan and local attack. End with a new voyage chosen freely, not a withheld rescue ending.

seasons.ending: Missing travelers rescued; raid repelled; trust damaged by real disclosures; Nix escapes after one limited act of repair. The Burrow chooses accountable outward partnerships.

seasons.title: Glass and Tides
seasons.question: Who owns a discovery?

episodes.title: A Map That Drinks
episodes.plot: Maela asks the travelers to verify a well claim; a glass storm destroys the easy route home.
episodes.character_turn: Madger accepts local leadership.

episodes.title: The Price of Shade
episodes.plot: Kavar offers water in exchange for exclusive certificates; the group shelters in a public court.
episodes.character_turn: Gorilla cannot solve scarcity by carrying more.

episodes.title: The Buried Lens
episodes.plot: A light impression appears to condemn Maela’s family; its angle proves the scene has been misread.
episodes.character_turn: Bot states what the image cannot establish.

episodes.title: A Table for Strangers
episodes.plot: A feast and comic cooking rivalry reveal whose labor maintains the public wells.
episodes.character_turn: A quiet bond replaces an exposition speech.

episodes.title: Below the Tide
episodes.plot: Toma takes the team to a drowned archive where the decisive record belongs to descendants.
episodes.character_turn: Madger gives up a claim he could legally seize.

episodes.title: The Captain’s Copy
episodes.plot: Toma’s stolen chart is exposed; a rival crew gets the rescue credit.
episodes.character_turn: Toma returns evidence without demanding praise.

episodes.title: Home Is Busy
episodes.plot: Mara, Jun and Pell resolve a festival dispute while the heroes are away.
episodes.character_turn: The town proves capable without its founder.

episodes.title: Water for No One
episodes.plot: Kavar’s debt forgery is proven, but the pump remains physically damaged.
episodes.character_turn: Victory requires repair and collective allocation.

episodes.title: The Open Court
episodes.plot: Public testimony and a difficult rebuild restore limited supply.
episodes.character_turn: Maela lets neighbors set the rules.

episodes.title: What the Map Leaves Out
episodes.plot: The travelers return with a route to Hushvale and news that some closures saved lives.
episodes.character_turn: Madger chooses a harder question over a triumphant legend.

seasons.ending: A public well restored, a stolen chart returned and a community given control of its own evidence.

seasons.title: The Necessary Cut
seasons.question: When does protection become control?

episodes.title: Weight of a Promise
episodes.plot: Eri refuses an overloaded departure and loses a prestigious contract.
episodes.character_turn: Gorilla respects a public refusal.

episodes.title: The Kind Captain
episodes.plot: Serik rescues stranded passengers and then demands permanent tribute.
episodes.character_turn: The team separates real skill from moral authority.

episodes.title: Three Islands, One Storm
episodes.plot: Rescue priorities divide dock crews as migration weather approaches.
episodes.character_turn: Eri launches with a bounded plan and turns back once.

episodes.title: A Song Without Purpose
episodes.plot: Bot composes music with sailmakers during repairs.
episodes.character_turn: He enjoys something nobody needs him to optimize.

episodes.title: The Voice in the Ice
episodes.plot: An echo seems to accuse the original routekeepers of betrayal.
episodes.character_turn: Ysolde distinguishes sequence from interpretation.

episodes.title: The Necessary Cut
episodes.plot: Independent measurements prove one closure still prevents a cascade.
episodes.character_turn: Madger abandons a simple reopening campaign.

episodes.title: The Forged Winter
episodes.plot: Ossa’s modern forged order is exposed beside genuine records.
episodes.character_turn: Ysolde publishes her own family’s benefit too.

episodes.title: Who Gets to Decide
episodes.plot: The archive order splits; local communities demand a role in testing.
episodes.character_turn: Expertise remains essential without becoming rule.

episodes.title: A Smaller Bridge
episodes.plot: A limited new crossing succeeds without reconnecting the dangerous chain.
episodes.character_turn: Gorilla teaches Tavi and accepts Eris’s lead.

episodes.title: The Road We Choose
episodes.plot: The team returns with a treaty of limited reciprocal routes.
episodes.character_turn: The world remains complex, but more people can shape their future.

seasons.ending: A dangerous closure remains; a forged one falls; a limited safe crossing replaces the fantasy of reopening everything.

seasons.title: The Sea Beneath
seasons.question: Can exchange happen without possession?

episodes.title: The Letter Below
episodes.plot: Namu invites an exchange after an old chart reappears.
episodes.character_turn: Bot asks what sharing requires.

episodes.title: Down Through Daylight
episodes.plot: A careful descent introduces an independent deep civilization.
episodes.character_turn: Madger becomes a guest.

episodes.title: The City on the Water
episodes.plot: A harbor festival reveals rival accounts of the city’s origins.
episodes.character_turn: No single record decides belonging.

episodes.title: Quiet Hull
episodes.plot: A rescue among bell-eels requires silence and patience.
episodes.character_turn: Snow remains on the safe shore with a familiar handler.

episodes.title: The Mineral Claim
episodes.plot: A surface syndicate uses an old charter to demand extraction.
episodes.character_turn: Toma renounces a profitable inherited claim.

episodes.title: No One’s Discovery
episodes.plot: Residents show the heroes that their map already names the supposedly lost shore.
episodes.character_turn: The expedition changes its language and purpose.

episodes.title: Heat and Distance
episodes.plot: Kesh negotiates work with neglected Cinder Cuts families.
episodes.character_turn: Apology precedes the new machine.

episodes.title: A Captain Without a Crew
episodes.plot: Brakka’s band fractures over burned supplies and unpaid shares.
episodes.character_turn: Dreg returns a victim ledger and accepts consequences.

episodes.title: The Shared Passage
episodes.plot: Partners establish a narrow, accountable trade route.
episodes.character_turn: Namu shares enough to cooperate while retaining boundaries.

episodes.title: A Place to Return To
episodes.plot: Visitors from several regions share an ordinary meal and exchange future invitations.
episodes.character_turn: Home grows through relationships, not conquest.

seasons.ending: A reciprocal deep-world partnership and a fractured raiding network create a new political landscape.

standalone_stories.title: The Empty Chair
standalone_stories.plot: Everyone leaves Gorilla a plate and nobody notices he has missed every meal. He must name his limit; friends must change the work, not merely deliver food.

standalone_stories.title: The Wrong Song
standalone_stories.plot: A route song is performed beautifully with one practical verse missing. The failure becomes a lesson in learning from people, not collecting exotic art.

standalone_stories.title: The Painted Door
standalone_stories.plot: A repaired door carries a former family’s mark. Ownership of the object and ownership of the memory pull in different directions.

standalone_stories.title: Snow’s Long Morning
standalone_stories.plot: A largely wordless walk follows an innocent smell, a lost glove and a tired visitor. The audience learns to read her pauses before the people do.

standalone_stories.title: The Cup That Leaked
standalone_stories.plot: A contest rewards an elegant cup until it is filled. The apprentice who admits a flaw wins no prize but earns a better commission.

standalone_stories.title: When the Founder Visits
standalone_stories.plot: Madger returns to Reedbank expecting to help and finds a community busy without him. He must learn how to be a son on a quiet day.

standalone_stories.title: One Honest Bargain
standalone_stories.plot: Pip returns an object and loses three customers. Building a lawful stall is less glamorous and harder than one dramatic confession.

standalone_stories.title: The Unnecessary Tune
standalone_stories.plot: Bot shares a piece of music. Lume begins to debug it before realizing he wanted her to listen.

standalone_stories.title: A Night Without Lamps
standalone_stories.plot: A planned dark festival becomes a comic navigation problem for surface visitors; local expertise solves it before danger is invented.

standalone_stories.title: Seeds for a Rival
standalone_stories.plot: A failed harvest experiment can be saved only by sharing seeds with a competitor who was correct about its limits.

standalone_stories.title: The Faster Letter
standalone_stories.plot: A correction must catch a false story before a caravan acts. Lark wins by admitting her own role, while Tessera abandons a profitable identity.

standalone_stories.title: The Better Builder
standalone_stories.plot: A sibling contest becomes a public credit dispute. The winning structure is the one whose builders can explain each other’s contribution.

setpieces.title: The Root That Let Go
setpieces.setup: A crown begins its seasonal turn while a wagon is halfway across. The first warning is a cup sliding sideways, followed by a lashing tightening to a musical note. Nix reaches the far bank with the evidence case. Madger has one clear jump after them. Then Snow looks down: someone is trapped beneath the wagon.
setpieces.action: Gorilla braces a temporary anchor, Bot fixes a tether to an existing ring, and Senn names the root that will release next. Madger abandons pursuit and descends. The rescue succeeds because each partner solves a different physical problem. The case leaves with Nix.
setpieces.lasting_result: A rescued traveler remembers the direction of the lost convoy. The heroes lose the easy proof but gain a person and a harder route forward.

setpieces.title: The Storm of False Suns
setpieces.setup: A glass storm scatters sunset into dozens of apparent horizons. The caravan’s packbeasts refuse the glittering shortcut. Madger mistakes refusal for fear until a glassback drake rises beneath the thin crust.
setpieces.action: Maela leads everyone toward exposed bedrock while Gorilla shields the smallest travelers with a broken cargo panel. Bot cannot trust visual bearings. Lark drops bright cloth markers that work only at close range. The team must leave a valuable crate behind to keep the water load.
setpieces.lasting_result: The lost crate contains Maela’s best instrument. At Ossara she must prove her case with testimony and a cruder shared tool.

setpieces.title: An Hour Below the Sea
setpieces.setup: The tide exposes the archive steps. Inside, light ripples over a ceiling painted with familiar family names. Toma finds the sought charter and an older ownership record he would prefer to leave. A reefback’s passage changes the current sooner than expected.
setpieces.action: The party must carry people and records up separate intact stairs. Madger cannot take both a heavy proof chest and an injured rival; he chooses the rival. Toma removes the chest’s useful sheets, leaves the valuable fittings and loses his salvage profit.
setpieces.lasting_result: The rival confirms the rescue and the archive’s provenance. Evidence survives without making the heroes owners of the place.

setpieces.title: The Island That Tilted
setpieces.setup: During a crowded festival, an overloaded cargo platform begins to tilt toward the cloud sea. Serik offers the only nearby ship, on terms that would bind the dock to him. Eri knows his craft cannot safely take the advertised load.
setpieces.action: She divides the rescue between an existing sheltered deck and a smaller craft, using counterweights to hold the platform while people cross. Gorilla must release an empty cargo section instead of trying to save everything. A storm manta’s wake provides a brief calm interval, not a miraculous obedient rescue.
setpieces.lasting_result: Everyone reaches refuge; expensive freight is lost. Serik cannot sell his false heroic story to people who watched the actual choice.

setpieces.title: The Voice Beyond the Warmth
setpieces.setup: A familiar voice calls from the ice, repeating an intimate sentence in the wrong rhythm. The group almost follows it beyond the warm ridge. Ysolde hears the same breath twice and recognizes a copied fragment.
setpieces.action: A choirwraith emerges against the aurora like torn translucent cloth. Warmth weakens its membranes, but the portable heater has a finite charge. The team moves together between marked refuges rather than scattering toward voices.
setpieces.lasting_result: Bot preserves the sound with its uncertainty attached. The incident prepares the audience to question a later echo record without dismissing all old evidence.

setpieces.title: The Small Bridge
setpieces.setup: The final crossing is smaller and less glorious than the restored ancient span Madger imagined. During its first test, one bearing shifts. A crowd waits for Gorilla to hold the structure by force.
setpieces.action: He stops the test, orders the empty span unloaded and lets Eris direct the correction. Tavi admits his measurement was copied from the wrong revision. Their public delay costs a day of celebration and prevents a private disaster.
setpieces.lasting_result: The opening is earned through changed behavior. Oren names the entire crew when the first travelers cross.

setpieces.title: The Silent Hull
setpieces.setup: A rescue boat must pass a bell-eel nesting channel with a damaged propeller that strikes the hull. The creature’s resonators glow one after another beneath the water, revealing its enormous length.
setpieces.action: Namu orders the engine stopped. Toma uses the current; Madger and Gorilla shift weight slowly instead of rowing harder. Bot shuts down an unnecessary vibrating pump. The trapped travelers must trust a boat that appears to be doing nothing.
setpieces.lasting_result: The rescue succeeds without defeating the animal. A damaged hull and missed tide force the party to stay in Lumen Tide long enough to understand its conflict.

setpieces.title: The Fire Brakka Ordered
setpieces.setup: Brakka orders captured food burned to prove she cannot be challenged. Heat draws an ashmaw toward the freight yard and cuts off her own crew’s retreat. Dreg sees supplies for his relatives among the crates.
setpieces.action: He opens a civilian escape lane and refuses the order. Vessa guides workers along the mapped foot path. Kesh’s crew cools a diversion trench while the heroes move people away from the heat. Brakka escapes with a smaller loyal band, stripped of the claim that she protects the district.
setpieces.lasting_result: Dreg gives up the victim ledger. Returning stolen goods and testifying become the beginning of change, not an instant pardon.
